issues.problem: The child is alone at a screen; there may be no friend to wave to.
issues.suggestion: Wave to Tom.

issues.problem: Same problem: no friend is with the child at the screen.
issues.suggestion: Smile at Anna.

issues.problem: PREA1-10 (copy words) is not practised: no command asks the child to copy a word.
issues.suggestion: Replace commands[5] with the line below so PREA1-10 is practised, or remove PREA1-10.

issues.problem: 'Say a word.' is too open for a 6-year-old beginner; they will not know which word to say.
issues.suggestion: Write the word cat.

issues.problem: 'Clap three.' is not natural English.
issues.suggestion: Clap three times.

issues.problem: PREA1-02 (respond to simple questions) is not practised; the lesson has no questions. The child names numbers and things.
'She counts thirteen, fourteen, fifteen fish' is confusing: counting seems to start at thirteen.
issues.suggestion: She counts the fish. There are fifteen fish!

issues.problem: 'Sam has sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty balls.' is not correct English and is confusing.
issues.suggestion: Sam counts his balls. Sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty!

issues.problem: 'Show me fifteen.' cannot be done with fingers (a child has ten).
issues.suggestion: Point to the number fifteen.

issues.problem: Drawing twelve flowers takes too long for a 6-year-old in a listen-and-do lesson.
issues.suggestion: Count the flowers.

issues.problem: 'Say how many.' is unclear: how many of what?
issues.suggestion: Count the birds.

issues.problem: 'Say your colour.' is unclear; a child has no 'own' colour.
issues.suggestion: Say your favourite colour.

issues.problem: 'brother' is a lesson word but is not in the story.
issues.suggestion: Sam has a brother and a baby sister.

issues.problem: 'Find the sister.' repeats 'Show me the baby.' (the sister is the baby); 'brother' is never practised in the commands.
issues.suggestion: Find the brother.

issues.problem: 'Tom has a happy body.' is not natural English; the story also never uses 'feet'.
issues.suggestion: He can jump with his feet. Tom is happy.

issues.problem: 'arm' is a lesson word but is not in the story.
issues.suggestion: He can wave with his hand and his arm.

issues.problem: We clap two hands; 'clap your hand' is wrong.
issues.suggestion: Hand, hand, clap your hands.

issues.problem: 'feet, feet, feet' has no meaning and breaks the 'this is my...' pattern.
issues.suggestion: Leg, leg, foot, foot, these are my feet.

issues.problem: PREA1-02 (respond to simple questions) is not practised; there are no questions. The child names body parts ('Say hand').
A child cannot look at their own ear.
issues.suggestion: Point to your ears.

issues.problem: 'ear' is a lesson word but is not in the story.
issues.suggestion: She has two eyes, two ears and a small nose.

issues.problem: 'mouth' is a lesson word but is not in the story.
issues.suggestion: She smiles with her mouth. Lucy is happy.

issues.problem: We see with two eyes; singular sounds wrong.
issues.suggestion: Eyes, eyes, I see with my eyes.

issues.problem: We listen with two ears; singular sounds wrong.
issues.suggestion: Ears, ears, I listen with my ears.

issues.problem: 'skirt' and 'jacket' are lesson words but are not in the chant; 'skirt' is also not in the story, so 'Look at the skirt.' comes from nowhere.
issues.suggestion: Skirt and jacket, shoes and jeans.

issues.problem: The lesson word 'clothes' is not in the story.
issues.suggestion: They like their clothes. They go to the park.

issues.problem: 'Put the pen here.' is unclear at a screen: where is 'here'?
issues.suggestion: Put your pen on your desk.

issues.problem: PREA1-02 (respond to simple questions) is not practised; there are no questions. The child names classroom things ('Say chair').
